subject: Hospitality
title: Robot Kitchens and Automation
description: A quick win: understand Robot Kitchens and Automation.

hook.text: Flippy the robot can cook 300 burgers an hour without breaks, complaints, or sick days. It never asks for a raise.

buildup.text: Automation targets the most repetitive kitchen tasks: frying, assembling bowls, making coffee, and flipping burgers.

discovery.text: Restaurant labor shortages accelerated robotic adoption. When you can't hire humans, machines become the solution.

twist.text: Robot kitchens struggle with complex dishes, custom orders, and the improvisation that makes a great cook irreplaceable.

climax.text: The future kitchen likely blends both: robots for repetitive tasks, humans for creativity and personal touch.

punchline.text: Robots flip burgers; humans create menus. The kitchen will be hybrid.

quiz.question: What accelerated the adoption of robots in restaurant kitchens?
options: Labor shortages—restaurants couldn't hire enough human workers
